messages.subject: map extension
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering if anyone had any ideas as to why a chromosome on a genetic map would become more distended on removing (potentially) problematic markers than before. I have a vexing situation where I have one badly elongated chromosome on a genetic map. I selected a subset of the markers on that chromosome to remove, but after doing so, the elongation on that chromosome became worse rather than better as I had expected. Interestingly, the number of breakpoints on that chromosome is comparable to the expected number of breakpoints for that chromosome, and to the number on the non-distended chromosomes. Essentially, it appears as though there are two linkage groups on the one chromosome. Any insights into this phenomena would be much appreciated. 

Thanks very much,
Jen

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] map extension
parts:
It's rather difficult to tell without further details. After removing the problematic markers, do you have two sets of markers that are each well behaved but with a very large gap between them?

If you have nothing to close the gap between the two sets of markers, I'd just split the chromosome into two linkage groups (e.g., 1a and 1b)

karl
